messages.content: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite located at latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. Don't give me hourly information

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content: I’m ready to pull the forecast for you, but I need the longitude of the campsite. Could you let me know the longitude (in decimal degrees) so I can fetch the next 10 days of daily maximum temperature (in °F) and total precipitation (in inches)?
message.reasoning:
The user wants weather forecast for a campsite at latitude 35. and longitude? They didn't provide longitude. They said "latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days". Probably missing longitude. We need to ask for longitude. Also they want daily temperature and precipitation forecasts, temperature 2m max in Fahrenheit, sum of precipitation in inches. They don't want hourly info.

We need to fetch data from Open-Meteo API. The function requires latitude and longitude. We need to ask for missing longitude. Also we need to specify units: temperature unit=fahrenheit, precipitation unit=inch? Open-Meteo supports precipitation unit in mm. We can convert to inches. But we can request precipitation_sum in mm and then convert. Or we can request precipitation_sum in mm and then convert to inches. The API supports precipitation_sum. We can request daily=temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum. Units: temperature_unit=fahrenheit, precipitation_unit=inch? Let's check Open-Meteo docs: precipitation_unit can be mm or inch. Yes, precipitation_unit=inch. So we can request precipitation_sum in inches. Good.

We need to request daily=temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum. Also we need to set timezone? Not necessary. We need to set forecast days: 10 days. The API supports "forecast_days" parameter. So we can set forecast_days=10.

We need to call the function with appropriate params. But we need latitude and longitude. Since missing longitude, we should ask user for it.
